identity.title: Food Safety Plan for Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips

scan.summary: This is a Food Safety Plan under the FDA's Preventive Controls for Human Food rule (21 CFR Part 117), prepared by a PCQI and approved by the plant manager. It describes the company's hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, and supply-chain program for refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips made at the Salem facility. The plan is the company's binding statement of how it will ensure food safety and is enforceable by FDA and Oregon Department of Agriculture.
scan.freshness_note: The plan is dated May 12, 2025, and is currently in effect. At today's date (2026-09-27), the plan is over one year old. For a document that may address changing conditions (personnel, suppliers, equipment), you may wish to review whether updates are due, but no renewal date is stated in the document.

gaps.title: Blast chiller temperature monitoring may miss early-phase cooling
gaps.description: The plan states the blast chiller operator records temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours, but does not specify how temperature is measured during the critical early phase (135°F to 70°F in 2 hours). If only spot checks are made at the 2-hour mark, the operator cannot know whether the critical limit was met continuously. 21 CFR 121.135(a) requires monitoring procedures that ensure critical limits are met during production.
gaps.fix: Add a description of the monitoring procedure: either continuous temperature logging on the blast chiller, or a defined schedule of checks (e.g., every 15 or 30 minutes) during the first 2 hours. Document what equipment is used and how the operator verifies the time-temperature path is met.
gaps.quote: The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling log.

gaps.title: No description of corrective action effectiveness testing
gaps.description: The plan describes corrective actions (re-cooking, re-swabbing, re-running through metal detector, etc.) but does not state how the company verifies that these actions actually eliminated the hazard or restored food safety. For example, if a cooling batch exceeds time limits and is discarded, there is no mention of testing or verification that the problem will not recur. 21 CFR 121.140(a) requires corrective actions to be effective in ensuring the food is safe.
gaps.fix: For each corrective action, add a sentence stating how effectiveness is verified. Examples: 'Product re-cooked to 212°F for 60 minutes is verified safe by checking the cook log and thermometer calibration record.' 'If a Listeria spp. swab is positive, product is held until the follow-up swab confirms the surface is negative.' 'If cooling time is exceeded, the batch is discarded and the blast chiller is checked by maintenance before the next batch.'
gaps.quote: If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or discarded, and the cause is recorded.

gaps.title: Listeria environmental monitoring frequency may be insufficient
gaps.description: The plan states 'Listeria spp. swabs, 10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2' as the sanitation control, and section 7 states 'Environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly.' However, for a ready-to-eat product with a 45-day shelf life and Listeria identified as a significant hazard at multiple steps (blending/filling, refrigerated storage), weekly environmental monitoring alone may not meet the requirement under 21 CFR 121.150(a) to establish a frequency adequate to detect and prevent Listeria contamination. The plan does not justify why weekly is sufficient or whether additional frequency is needed based on product characteristics, production volume, or history.
gaps.fix: Add text justifying the weekly frequency: 'Weekly environmental monitoring is based on the 45-day product shelf life and the risk of post-cook environmental contamination. Swab results are reviewed within seven working days and trended quarterly to detect any trend toward increased contamination. If any positive Listeria spp. result is detected, the frequency is increased to [specify, e.g., daily or twice weekly] until the source is eliminated.' Alternatively, increase the stated frequency if weekly is insufficient for your product line and distribution.
gaps.locator: Section 4 (Preventive controls), Listeria row, and Section 7 (Verification)
gaps.quote: Listeria spp. swabs, 10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2

Suppliers that do not meet these criteria are removed from the approved list and products from such suppliers are not accepted.'

gaps.title: Recall plan not described
gaps.description: The plan does not include a recall plan as required by 21 CFR 121.160(a). The plan describes corrective actions and records but does not address how the company would identify affected product, notify customers or regulators, or coordinate a recall if a safety issue is discovered.
gaps.fix: Add a new section, 'Recall Plan,' describing: (1) the person or team responsible for initiating and managing a recall; (2) how affected product will be identified (e.g., by date code, batch number, or lot); (3) how the company will notify customers, retailers, and the FDA or Oregon Department of Agriculture; (4) how product will be recovered and destroyed or salvaged; (5) how the company will document the recall and verify effectiveness; and (6) how frequently the recall plan is tested [specify, e.g., annually]. Reference or attach the detailed recall procedure.

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.

5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
